name: Xia Shiyong
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2007) as a shareholder of Kingfa Sci. & Tech. (600143.SH); current role not confirmed
profile: Appeared on the 2007 Hurun China list with wealth from Kingfa Sci. & Tech., the Guangzhou modified-plastics maker founded in 1993 by Yuan Zhimin. Searches of current Kingfa filings and board lists did not surface him, so his present role and status could not be verified.
notes: Very low public footprint; no current Kingfa board listing found. Best route would be via Kingfa's board secretary/IR office, but verify his connection first.

name: Sanjeev Kanoria
current_role: Owner & Chairman, Advinia Health Care (UK); Vice-Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Austrian Anadi Bank
profile: London-based liver transplant surgeon turned entrepreneur. Ex-McKinsey (healthcare), he co-founded UK care-home operator Advinia Health Care in 1999 and in 2013 bought Hypo Alpe Adria's Austrian banking unit (renamed Austrian Anadi Bank) via Anadi Financial Holdings for about EUR 65.5m.
interesting_fact: A trained liver transplant/HPB surgeon (FRCS, PhD from UCL on reducing liver injury) who became a European bank owner; he co-authored the liver chapter in the 26th edition of Bailey & Love's surgery textbook.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 Advinia became the first UK care provider to research robots in care homes, joining the EU-Japan CARESSES project that gave SoftBank's Pepper robot culturally competent AI for older people.
notes: Brother of Hemant Kanoria (SREI). Hurun lists him under India; he is UK-based. Best route likely via Advinia Health Care's corporate office (advinia.co.uk) - no published personal contact found.

name: Sajan Kumar Bansal
profile: Commerce graduate who in 1981 incorporated Skipper Investments Ltd, later Skipper Steels and then Skipper Ltd. Starting with steel poles for telecom, he built Skipper into a major Indian maker of power transmission & distribution towers, plus polymer pipes; he still runs it as CMD.
interesting_fact: Skipper began as a small maker of 'Hamilton' steel poles for telecom connectivity and became a leading supplier of telecom poles and masts in India in the 1980s-90s before pivoting to power transmission towers.
notes: Skipper's T&D tower business is directly relevant to grid/energy-infrastructure topics. mail@ is the company's general inbox, not personal. Also Managing Trustee of Skipper Foundation.

name: Han Hui
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2007) with wealth from 'Silver Land Hotel'; current role not verified
profile: Appeared once on the 2007 Hurun China list with hotel-industry wealth attributed to 'Silver Land Hotel' (likely 银地酒店). Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable profile linking 韩辉 to this hotel, so identity and current status could not be confirmed.
notes: Common name and only a single 2007 list appearance; could not identify which Han Hui this is. Not recommended for outreach without further verification.

name: Li Binghe
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2008) with Saifeiya Group (Inner Mongolia duck farming/restaurants); current role not verified
profile: Appeared on the 2008 Hurun China list with wealth from Saifeiya Group (内蒙古塞飞亚), a vertically integrated meat-duck company in Ningcheng County, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia, spanning breeding, farming, slaughtering, cooked food and feed. Current Saifeiya filings name 李槟全 as legal representative/chairman; the name 李秉和 could not be found, so this may be a transliteration variant.
interesting_fact: Saifeiya breeds its own duck lines from great-grandparent stock down to commercial ducks, and in 2019 struck a strategic partnership with Country Garden to scale up; its products are export-certified for Japan and Korea.
notes: Possible that Hurun's 'Li Binghe' is Li Binquan (李槟全), Saifeiya's chairman and head of the poultry branch of the China Animal Agriculture Association - unverified. Confirm the name before using.

name: Narendra Aggarwal
current_role: Chairman, Shivalik Group / Shivalik Prints Ltd (per 2017 reporting); registry data suggests he may have left the board
profile: Patriarch of the Aggarwal family behind Shivalik Prints, a Faridabad (Delhi NCR) knitwear and garment exporter founded in 1998 as a small family business; it now runs about nine factories supplying Walmart, GAP, H&M, Target and others. Sons/younger directors including Nishant Aggarwal (MD) now lead day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Shivalik's factories all sit within a 4-5 km radius so orders can be processed within six hours; in 2017 it produced ~200,000 knitted garments a day with a 99.8% on-time shipping record and zero air shipments.
deep_cut_fact: Shivalik runs 1.5 MW of solar generation with water recycling and set out to become the largest biologically zero-discharge apparel factory in Haryana.
notes: Hurun shares the wealth with Mukesh Aggarwal. The enquiry@ address is the company's general inbox. Next generation (Nishant Aggarwal, MD) may be the more active contact.

name: Robert James Gamgort
current_role: Director, Sherwin-Williams; former Chairman/CEO of Keurig Dr Pepper (left KDP board March 31, 2026)
profile: Consumer-goods CEO who ran Pinnacle Foods (2009-16, led its 2013 IPO), then Keurig Green Mountain for JAB and, from 2018, the merged Keurig Dr Pepper as CEO and later chairman. He handed the CEO job to Tim Cofer in 2024, served as non-employee chairman until March 2026, and now sits on Sherwin-Williams' board.
interesting_fact: Before packaged food he was President of Major League Baseball Properties, credited with rebuilding baseball's marketing after the 1994 players' strike, then ran marketing for M&M/Mars and Mars' North American business.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in marketing at General Foods (later Kraft), and studied at the London School of Economics alongside his Bucknell economics BA before a Kellogg MBA.
notes: KDP 2026 proxy confirms he stepped off the KDP board effective March 31, 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1418135/000119312526177266/d201572ddef14a.htm); KDP IR is therefore only an indirect route. No personal published contact found.

name: William John Sibold
current_role: President and CEO, Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (since Sept 2023)
profile: Bill Sibold spent ~12 years at Sanofi, ending as EVP Specialty Care and President of Sanofi North America, after roles at Biogen and Avanir. He joined Madrigal in 2023 and led the launch of Rezdiffra (resmetirom), the first FDA-approved drug for MASH/NASH liver disease, approved in March 2024.
interesting_fact: At Sanofi he is credited with bringing Dupixent to market and building specialty care into Sanofi's largest global business unit; he called Dupixent 'a once-in-a-career type of product' in a 2020 interview.
deep_cut_fact: Marking the 30th anniversary of Sanofi's Rare Humanitarian Program in 2021, he highlighted that '95 percent of known rare diseases still lack an approved treatment.'
notes: Madrigal is based in West Conshohocken, PA. Media contact named in releases: Christopher Frates.

name: Li Guodong
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chairman, Win Hanverky Holdings Ltd (永嘉集團, HKEX: 3322)
profile: Li Kwok Tung Roy (李國棟, Mandarin: Li Guodong), 75, co-founded Hong Kong-based Win Hanverky (Yongjia Group), an OEM manufacturer of sportswear and outdoor apparel for international brands that also runs a fashion brands & licensing business. He has 45+ years in the apparel industry and remains chairman, holding his stake via Quinta Asia Ltd (70%).
interesting_fact: Win Hanverky has run its OEM manufacturing business for over 45 years, making apparel for internationally renowned sports and outdoor brands and selling mainly into Europe, the US and mainland China.
deep_cut_fact: He and his co-founder and deputy chairman Lai Ching Ping are both 75 and both joined the board in December 2005; they still co-own the controlling vehicle Quinta Asia Ltd on a 70/30 split.

public_contacts.value: Strategic Financial Relations Ltd (Ms. Veron Ng), IR/media enquiries, +852 2864 4831

notes: Hurun's 'Li Guodong / Yongjia Group' matched to Li Kwok Tung Roy of Win Hanverky (永嘉集團) via Cantonese/Mandarin transliteration; Lixinger lists 李國棟 as largest shareholder of 03322.HK. Day-to-day operations now led by a new CEO appointed March 2026.

name: Prudence E Carlson
current_role: Non-independent Director (since 2008), Telephone and Data Systems (TDS); Trustee of the TDS Voting Trust; private investor
profile: Prudence E. Carlson, 74, is a member of the Carlson family that controls Chicago-based Telephone and Data Systems through the TDS Voting Trust, of which she is a trustee. A Harvard BA and private investor, she has sat on the TDS board since 2008 alongside her siblings, including chair and CEO Walter C.D. Carlson.
interesting_fact: TDS's board includes four Carlson siblings - LeRoy T. Carlson Jr., Walter C.D. Carlson (Chair/CEO), Dr. Letitia G. Carlson and Prudence - reflecting the family's control of the telecom group through the TDS Voting Trust.

public_contacts.value: elsa.ansani@tdsinc.com (TDS Corporate Secretary - published channel for communications to individual directors)

notes: Very private; no public profile beyond TDS proxy. The 2026 proxy says interested parties may contact any individual director via the Corporate Secretary - that is the only published route.

name: John F Rex
current_role: Strategic Advisor, UnitedHealth Group (since Sept 2, 2025); formerly President and CFO
profile: John Rex joined UnitedHealth in 2012 as CFO of Optum, became group CFO in 2016 and added the title of President in April 2024. In September 2025, amid a leadership overhaul under returning CEO Stephen Hemsley, he handed the CFO role to Wayne DeVeydt and became a strategic advisor.
interesting_fact: Before UnitedHealth he was a Wall Street equity research analyst covering managed care and health-care facilities (JPMorgan, previously Bear Stearns) - he went from analysing insurers like UnitedHealth to running its finances.
deep_cut_fact: He is a certified public accountant with a dual bachelor's in accounting and economics from Brigham Young University and a Wharton MBA (finance), and also worked as a strategy and operations consultant.
notes: Role change confirmed in UNH 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000110465926046125/tm261387-6_def14a.htm). UNH is under heavy media scrutiny; a strategic-advisor executive is unlikely to do press without corporate approval.
